old: It's named for a body part that was, quite literally, cut short.
The first half of its name describes a docked or cropped tail.
A trademarked yellow loader shares its name with this short-tailed wildcat.
clues: This wild animal of North America is named for a plain description of one body part, the very feature that makes its silhouette look cut short.
A spotted, tufted-eared wildcat roughly twice the size of a house cat, with a stubby tail; it is smaller and far more widespread than its northern cousin, the lynx.
Builders also use its name for a small skid-steer loader, after a trademark passed into everyday use. It shares a root with a short, cropped haircut.
